business_problem: Rakuten needed to ship faster, recover from incidents faster, and increase autonomous execution across a large engineering organization without relaxing security or reliability standards.
solution_summary: Rakuten made Codex a core part of its engineering stack and aligned its rollout around three operational goals: build faster, build safer, and operate smarter. For speed, Codex works with KQL-based monitoring and diagnostics so engineers can move from alert to root-cause analysis and remediation more quickly, cutting mean time to recovery roughly in half. For safety, Codex is invoked directly in CI/CD pipelines for code review and vulnerability checks against Rakuten's internal coding principles, allowing guardrails to run before code reaches production. For autonomy, Codex is used on larger, ambiguously specified projects, where it can move from partial requirements to working implementations, as shown by a full-stack mobile project with a Python/FastAPI backend and a Swift/SwiftUI app. Rakuten pairs these workflows with workshops across teams, shifting engineers toward writing better specifications and verification standards rather than reviewing every line by hand.
